items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I had the pleasure of having lunch with Queen Alia in Jordan.

ctx.x: People have said that there’s a difference in the way the music is approached and—

Well music gets you in many places that you would never think that you would be in. Like in school I used to read about Egypt, the pyramids and places like that. Turkey, Istanbul. And I’m a frustrated tourist. My girlfriend, she made me a frustrated tourist. Well she’s an English professor. And of course I used to go there and never see anything. But when she came over with me she had an itinerary made out, we’d go to this place, this place, go to Marseilles, go to see Versailles, go to, oh my goodness, the…
you know. And I have enjoyed it. I have really, really enjoyed being in the music business. I thank God every night for giving me the talent and blessing me.

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Then from Pakistan, we went to Amman, Jordan, and we had lunch with the late Queen Alia

ctx.x: Would you just play for an hour or something?

We would play 45-minute concert and take a little intermission and take another 45 minutes. Very easy. Oh, very easy, but the people absolutely just went wild. Of course, Louie Armstrong and Duke had been going over there for a long time. Louie Armstrong was the first one to start going over. Then from Pakistan, we went to Amman, Jordan, and we had lunch with the late Queen Alia (PHONETIC) and Princess --
Did you meet Hussein, King Hussein?
